title: Tracker to fix failing tests due to the new random image ID
body:
We are tentatively introducing a new random image ID in [container-libs](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1346).
Here's the PR used to find the tests: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/30176
This issue will be used to track failing tests happened on podman:

[testing-farm:fedora-${version}-${arch}:podman-fedora]
- [x] `podman load - by image name`
- [x] `podman load - from URL`
- [ ] `podman pull with policy flag` 
  Not sure this is related. Might be a flaky test.
- [ ] `podman image scp transfer`
  This can't be fixed test-side. The test fails only as a side effect of `podman image scp` now creating a second image record for content already in the store, and that duplication is user-visible well beyond this test: a plain podman pull of an image the user already has does the same thing and leaves the original record dangling as `<none>:<none>`. The fix belongs in container-libs, the "is this content already here?" check consults only the new matching-digest index, so it never matches images created before the change (or by skopeo/buildah), which store that same content digest as their ID.
- [ ] `podman images -a, after pulling by sha`
   This can't be fixed test-side: the test asserts exactly the property that brok, that pulling an image already in the store still shows one image, not two (its own comment: "podman recognizes it as the same image … still only shows us one image"). It now shows a duplicate (`quay.io/libpod/testimage  <none>  d5f3ea6c0cbd`) because the dedup check consults only the new matching-digest index and never matches records written before the change (skopeo/buildah/older podman), whose content digest is stored as their ID. 
- [ ] `image events`
   This can't be fixed test-side: It fails only because `podman load` of an already-present image creates a second record which takes over the image's name, leaving the original as `<none>:<none>`: every later `$IMAGE` command then reports the new record's ID, and `rmi` of the original emits no `untag` events at all (10 event lines instead of 11). Encoding that into the expected event stream would assert the buggy behaviour as the contract.
- [ ] `podman push and search ok with --tls-verify=false`
   This can't be fixed test-side: `iid` is captured at runtime so random IDs are fine, a control run with a dedup-capable store passes and leaves a single record. It fails only because pulling back the pushed image creates a duplicate record instead of reusing the existing one.
- [ ] `podman push and search ok with --tls-verify=true`
  Same as above.
- [ ] `podman-auto-update --authfile`
  Not a test bug: the duplicate record splits the image's manifest digests across two entries and the re-tag points the name at the one lacking the registry's digest, so auto-update sees a phantom update. The test is correctly flagging that, and the fix belongs in container-libs.
- [ ] `sdnotify : ignore`
  Not related to this topic, but we can fix it by adding `_prefetch $IMAGE` before `podman create` command to avoid filling the `cid` variable with unwanted output.
- [ ] `podman image mount`
   Not a test bug: It fails because the duplicate record makes image mount -a list two entries for one image, and the untagged one sorts first (hex IDs sort before quay.io/…), which breaks the expr-anchored match. Both rows point at the same mount path, one image stored twice. Loosening the matcher would accept a user's image being mounted twice under two identities.
- [ ] `podman checkpoint --export, with volumes`
  This can't be fixed test-side: there is no image-ID comparison in the test, it fails inside `podman container restore --import` itself, with locating image with ID "b82e560ed57b…": image not known. A checkpoint archive embeds the source store's RootfsImageID, and restore looks that exact ID up in the destination store without re-resolving it after the by-name pull. Image IDs are now random and therefore store-local, so the same image has a different ID on every machine.

[bud local/remote root fedora-current / lima]
- [ ] `bud with --layers and --no-cache flags`
- [ ] `bud-no-change`
- [ ] `bud with FROM --after`

[int local/remote root/rootless ${os}-${version} / lima]
- [x] `Podman create` fixed by c826ec4faaa21de64628757e05b35935d98ddfe1
  - [x] `[It] podman create using image list by digest`
  - [x] `[It] podman create using image list by tag`
  - [x] `[It] podman create using image list instance by digest`
  - [x] `[It] podman create using cross-arch image list instance by digest`
- [x] `Podman save` fixed by ffd9575d8679b22a86938c11e3b6d851b4956b30
  - [x] `[It] podman save --multi-image-archive (untagged images)`
- [x] `Podman images` fixed by 7a0a4396dd93a291ce7e574b4e4d93608360291a
  - [x] `[It] podman images with multiple tags`
  - [x] `[It] podman images filter by image name`
- [x] `Podman rmi`
    - [x] `[It] podman rmi image that is created from another named imaged`
- [x] `Podman pull` fixed by c91ee48c8949ab07942dfb638d66e5dde8a4f944
  - [x] `[It] podman pull by digest (image list)`
  - [x] `[It] podman pull by instance digest (image list)`
  - [x] `[It] podman pull by tag (image list)`

[sys local/remote root/rootless ${os}-${version} / lima]
almost the same as [testing-farm:fedora-${version}-${arch}:podman-fedora]
- [ ] `podman pull - EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC`
  Not sure this is related. Might be a flaky test.

[docker_py root fedora-current / lima]
- [ ] `TestImages.test_load_image`

I don't see a proper full CI run there yet, I would expect a lot more integration test failures. You likely only lock at packit which is not the main CI system, it is optional.
You need to get passed the "Validation" failure
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/43256000608/job/131314257498
